pages.page_summary: Nick rides the train with Tom from West Egg toward New York; as the train slows beside the valley of ashes, Nick observes the desolate dumping ground, the ash-men at work, and the looming eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg's billboard. When the train halts, Tom drunkenly seizes Nick's elbow and forces him off to meet his mistress.

pages.page_summary: Nick follows Tom over a railroad fence and down the road beneath the Eckleburg billboard to a small yellow-brick block of shops. They enter Wilson's garage, where Tom needles the ash-dusted proprietor about a car deal; then Myrtle Wilson descends the stairs and walks past her husband to meet Tom's eyes.

pages.page_summary: Past midnight in the apartment, Tom and Myrtle square off over Daisy's name; when Myrtle chants it, Tom breaks her nose with an open hand, and the room dissolves into bloody towels and wailing while McKee wakes, stares, and walks out. Nick retrieves his hat and follows, riding down with McKee in the elevator and accepting a vague lunch invitation; the night collapses into McKee in his underwear flipping a portfolio of photographic titles, and finally Nick half-asleep on a Pennsylvania Station bench at four in the morning.
